headline: Why energy costs matter far beyond the oil market
dek: Today's sample shows how the live app will look. Once automation is enabled, this file is replaced every morning.
story_title: Energy prices can ripple through inflation, currencies and interest rates
story_html: Energy prices are closely watched because their effects extend well beyond petrol stations. Persistently elevated energy costs can complicate central banks' efforts to bring inflation back toward target. In the United States, the Federal Reserve must weigh inflation risks against growth and employment. In Europe and the United Kingdom, household energy bills and industrial costs can shape both consumer confidence and policy expectations. Japan and South Korea are sensitive to import costs and exchange-rate movements, while China must balance domestic demand with global trade conditions.
b2_summary: When energy stays expensive, transport and production also cost more. This can keep prices high and make it harder for central banks to decide when to lower interest rates.

common_theme: Energy costs can influence inflation and interest-rate decisions across several major economies.

concept.title: How can energy prices spread through an economy?
concept.explanation: Energy is an input for transport, factories, heating and many services. If energy costs stay high, businesses may pass some of those costs on to consumers. That can keep inflation higher and influence central-bank decisions.

quiz.question: Why do central banks care about energy prices?
options: They can affect inflation across the economy.
quiz.explanation: Energy costs can spread into transport, production and consumer prices.

one_sentence: Persistently high energy costs can complicate central banks' efforts to bring inflation back toward target.
